statement:
Which of the following statements are true and which are false? Justify your answers.

(i) $a^{\ln b}=b^{\ln a}$ for all $a,b>0$.

(ii) $\cos(\sin\theta)=\sin(\cos\theta)$ for all real $\theta$.

(iii) There exists a polynomial $P$ such that $|P(\theta)-\cos\theta|\le10^{-6}$ for all real $\theta$.

(iv) $x^4+3+x^{-4}\ge5$ for all $x>0$.
solution:
(i) **True.** Taking logarithms,
$$\ln(a^{\ln b})=\ln b\cdot\ln a=\ln a\cdot\ln b=\ln(b^{\ln a}),$$
so $a^{\ln b}=b^{\ln a}$.

(ii) **False.** Take $\theta=0$: then $\cos(\sin0)=\cos0=1$, but $\sin(\cos0)=\sin1\approx0.84\ne1$. So the statement fails.

(iii) **False.** A non-constant polynomial is unbounded as $|\theta|\to\infty$, whereas $\cos\theta$ is bounded between $-1$ and $1$. No polynomial can approximate $\cos\theta$ to within $10^{-6}$ for *all* real $\theta$.

(iv) **True.** By AM-GM, $x^4+x^{-4}\ge2\sqrt{x^4\cdot x^{-4}}=2$, so $x^4+3+x^{-4}\ge2+3=5$ for all $x>0$.
hints: For (i), take logarithms of both sides.
For (ii) and (iii), find a counterexample or use boundedness.
For (iv), use AM-GM on x⁴ and x⁻⁴.
